Title: Ditch the Boss and Form a Worker Co-operative!

Presenter.Name: Esther Fraser for Game Makers 4 Co-operative Futures
Presenter.Bio: Esther Fraser is a hobbyist game-maker living in Halifax/Kjipuktuk. She sits on the steering committee of Game Makers 4 Co-operative Futures.

Description: What if we got to make games more like we play them: with meaningful choices? Worker co-operatives put game makers in the driver's seat. While co-ops can't change the economic reality of all society, they give worker-members the tools to respond in the ways that are best for them.

Title: Embodying Space & Place in Digital Worlds

Presenter.Name: Charlie MacLean
Presenter.Bio: Charlotte MacLean, otherwise known as Charlie, is an artist interested in horror, humour, and cross-disciplinary exploration. They graduated from NSCAD with a BFA in 2023 and have since spent most of their time working on a collaborative puppet real estate project about the recently demolished grassy field on Quinpool road. The project was workshopped during a 2024 CFAT Video Residency, adapted into a Beacon project for Nocturne 2025, exhibited at the Craig Gallery in 2026, and is currently undergoing a movie adaption. In 2025, during the Expanded Practice residency at DARC in Ottawa, Charlie used a greenscreen soundstage to produce an HTML-based point and click adventure starring a package delivery puppet named Palmstrom. Charlie works with a wide variety of media, including oil paint, Unity Game Engine, and cardboard. Their work explores themes of jobs, advertising, spaces, privilege, listlessness, impermanence, and desire.

Presenter.Name: Emily Flinn
Presenter.Bio: Emily Flinn is a Vietnamese Canadian interdisciplinary artist working in traditionally analogue mediums—oil painting, various printmaking techniques, and drawing materials. Currently, she is experimenting with media art mediums, in particular video games, and mixing her love of analogue mediums with her personal history and experience of growing up in a digital age. Flinn imbues her work with exeriences of the liminality and ambiguity she feels from her cultural identity and lived experiences. Though she explores personal subject matter and experiences that are oftentimes heavy, Flinn values adding a sense of humour, striking a balance of thoughtfulness and playful warmth. She is interested in themes pertaining to the physicality of the body, permanence versus temporality in physical space, and how these ideas both interact with memory and identity.

Presenter.Name: Derek Reilly
Presenter.Bio:
Derek Reilly is co-director of the Graphics and Experiential Media Lab within Dalhousie University‘s Faculty of Computer Science. They conduct research in the areas of mobile, ubiquitous, and embodied interaction, gaming and new media, mixed/virtual/augmented reality, and visualization.
They prioritise fun, playful explorations of new interaction modalities and novel scenarios for interaction with digital media and systems.  A major goal of the lab is to establish interactive techniques, paradigms, and toolkits that help designers of interactive systems consider the physical environment and our lived experience in these environments.

Presenter.Name: Dustin Harvey
Presenter.Bio:
Dustin Harvey is a Dartmouth-based artist working across film, theatre, and immersive performance. He is the founder of XOSECRET, where he creates participatory and site-responsive works presented across Canada and internationally. His work includes ALONE TOGETHER, a mobile app performance presented by SXSW, IDFA DocLab, MIT Docubase, and Belfast XR. His current mixed-reality project, AWAKE & STILL DROWNING, was presented at the Guanajuato International Film Festival, where it received the Best VR Experience award.

Across his work, Dustin is interested in what happens when an audience is given something to do: a simple instruction, a role to play, a place to go, or another person to pay attention to.

Presenter.Name: ray
Presenter.Bio:
Ray (they/them) is an artist and cultural worker based in Montreal. Their work includes interactive media, coded websites, zines, and community-engaged projects. Ray focuses on building work that emphasizes intimacy, care, and accessibility, and explores how technology shapes emotional and social life.

They use DIY and poetic coding methods to create small interactive tools and participatory experiences. Ray’s background in facilitation, social practice and public programming informs their collaborative approach to working with communities and collectives. 🌀 learning → making → teaching as a spiral.

Title: A million mom games

Presenter.Name: Sabrina Doiron
Presenter.Bio: Sabrina Doiron is a solo game developer and developing artist living in rural Nova Scotia/Mi'kma'ki with their family. They enjoy reading, mending and making both fabric and circuits, and are currently/always learning how to become themselves again. Their first and only exhibited work was a decade ago, but they're sharing their current process online at sabrinadoiron.blog.

Description: What makes a mom game? A million mom games is a self directed artist residency in motherhood making small games while meditating on and doing the care work of parenting. One part personal reflection on matrescence, one part field guide on the creative process during phases of transformation and upheaval.

Title: The Browser is Already a Game Engine: an invitation

Presenter.Name: Everest Pipkin
Presenter.Bio: Everest Pipkin is a writer, game developer, artist, and educator whose work both in the studio and in the garden follows themes of ecology, tool making, and fantasies of collapse and isolation– as well as the labor, maintenance, devotion, and collective care so often present in those fantasies. They produce printed material as books and zines, as well as digital work for the browser and in game engines. They also make drawings on paper.

Description: THE BROWSER IS ALREADY A GAME ENGINE argues that web browsers already possess most of the interactive, rendering, and interface elements that are used to define game engines. By centering hyperlinks and HTML DOM elements as core structures for interactivity and play, we'll talk about games that are websites, with all of the aesthetic particulars and social affordances built into the handmade web.
